Based on the web search results, here's what I found about Mistral Postgres backend, Vespa retrieval, context scoping, and queries documentation:

## Postgres Backend

The PostgreSQL (with the pgvector extension) backend is part of mistralai-search-toolkit. Dense (vector) search, hybrid (vector + full text) search, navigation, and partial updates are implemented.

## Context and Query Scoping

An important distinction exists between the Postgres and Vespa backends regarding context scoping:

IngestContext and RetrievalContext are accepted on every entrypoint and carried for propagation only, but this backend derives no scoping from them. In contrast, Vespa reads group_id off the context to scope a streaming-mode query (and refuses the query without one), and binds query_params into a schema's yql_filter.

## Protocol Implementation

PostgresStoreIndex implements the toolkit protocols VectorStoreIndex (dense and hybrid search, index, delete), NavigableIndex (navigate/read/grep/get_chunk), and PatchableIndex (partial updates).

The main takeaway is that while Vespa has built-in context scoping mechanisms for queries, the Postgres backend currently does not implement equivalent context protocols, which is an important consideration when switching between backends.

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

content.text:
No — the Postgres backend does not scope queries the way Vespa does.

- **Postgres backend**: `IngestContext` and `RetrievalContext` are accepted on every entrypoint of `PostgresStoreIndex`, but they're only carried through for propagation — the backend derives no actual query scoping from them.
- **Vespa backend**: actively uses the context — it reads `group_id` off the context to scope a streaming-mode query (and will refuse to run the query if `group_id` is missing), and binds `query_params` into the schema's `yql_filter`.

So if you're relying on `RetrievalContext` to isolate/filter results per group or tenant, that behavior is Vespa-specific — switching to Postgres won't give you the same isolation guarantees unless you add your own filtering (e.g., a WHERE clause or row-level security).
